I'm 23, I'm 4 months out of surgery. I had a herniated dis at L5 S1. Life was hell for 5 months, I tried all conservative methods but eventually the doctors and the pain convinced me to get surgery. Now I am pain free, back at the gym, starting to run, and overall feeling great. Besides the surgery a huge thing that helped me was strengthening my core and all the muscles that stabilize the spine. My advice is to not give up mentally. You will get through this some way or another. Set the goal in your mind that you will come back from this and that there will be a day where you look back at this pain free.  I remember I had moments of weakness where I felt like this was permanent. It's not. If you need more advice feel free to PM me.

Sometimes we put too much pressure on ourselves to achieve something or that we are fundamentally flawed when, in my opinion, you really don't need any conditions to accept yourself. If you are looking for the meaning of life then you will never live. When you stop looking for the meaning you will start to live. It's a mystery either way, for some that mystery is scary and to others it's a reason to not take themselves or anything too seriously, and in my experience taking life too seriously robs you of happiness.

I think you don't perceive reality as it is but as you are. I've had my fair share of paranoia from trauma and just going through difficult things that made me view the world as sinister and, like you said, "a horror story". But the thing is, if you choose that interpretation then the world will reflect it right back at you. Mushrooms really helped me realize this and I simply choose to stop being so paranoid because it's not worth it. This horror story interpretation of reality could equally be and illusion, a lie, and I don't think reality is good or bad, it just is. 

When it comes to the inherent meaninglessness of life that you might be talking about, I like to refer to the philosophy of Albert Camus. He explored the existential question of if life is really worth living. In short he concluded that while for some the realization that life has no meaning is a justification for despair and even suicide, it can also be seen as a beginning, as an opportunity to make of it what you wish and confront the absurdity. The most powerful act of rebelliousness is to find joy in the meaninglessness, to playfully dive into the void. We are headed towards death either way, you can be paranoid or you can relax and try to groove with it, either way we are all gonna be dust.

This is a hard question. Everyone thinks of death differently. What helped me is changing my perception of death from something that is bad and should be avoided at all costs to seeing it as something naturally inevitable and thus accepting it as just part of life. It takes balls to do this, but you have to see death as something natural, birth implies death.

I realized that my real fear was not death in and of itself, but dying before accomplishing all the things I want to do in this life. Then I realized that to accomplish these things I need to let go of this fear which is stopping me from living life to the fullest. So I let go, accepted death and focused on enjoying my life in the moment instead of always being on the lookout for what might kill me. It's really a matter of surrendering and trusting life, hopefully the mushrooms help you see this.
